correctness.rationale: Functional, inverse-functional, acyclic components are finite/omega/omega-star/Z directed paths. In a realizing order each component is convex. The adjacent-block boundary rule forbids exactly pairs with prior maximum and later minimum, forcing one distinct Z block between every two successive finite blocks; conversely ordering all omega blocks, then F blocks separated by Z, leftover Z, then omega-star blocks realizes all edges exactly. Deficit count follows from iff. Executed standalone checker confirms 494 type count multisets and 1364 strings, with no infinite inference from computations.

value.rationale: Provides a complete structural classification of the finitely-many-component exact-successor admissibility problem, the gap left by dense component completion. It identifies precisely why one-sided rays cannot buffer multiple finite paths and yields a sharp smallest number of two-sided infinite component buffers. This semantic boundary is a motivated invariant of ordered first-order structures rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
